readings.summary: Read the blueprint definition against Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, which the main theorem's type uses: for every s with ζ(s) = 0 that is not a trivial zero (s ≠ −2(n+1) for every natural n) and is not s = 1, Re s = 1/2. The blueprint's wording (every nontrivial zero lies on Re s = 1/2) matches. RiemannZetaZerosOnLine and Claim.Zeta are the project's restatements and unfold to the same condition. readings.summary: Read UpperTheory.EveryCharacter, Claim.HalfPlane and DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf. All three say: for every modulus N ≥ 1, every Dirichlet character χ mod N (primitive or not) and every s with Re s > 1/2, L(χ, s) ≠ 0, except when χ = 1 and s = 1. The Lean writes the exception as (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1). This matches the blueprint, including that imprimitive characters are covered.

readings.summary: Read UpperTheory.zeta_ne_zero_of_everyCharacter: from EveryCharacter it gives ζ(s) ≠ 0 for Re s > 1/2, s ≠ 1. The proof specialises to the trivial character mod 1 and rewrites with Mathlib's LFunction_modOne_eq (the L-function of the character mod 1 is ζ). That is exactly the blueprint's one-line proof.

readings.summary: Read Formalism.VW.critLine and gammaFactor_ne_zero. The argument: for primitive χ and 0 < Re s < 1 with L(χ, s) = 0, the gamma factor (Gammaℝ(s) or Gammaℝ(s+1), by parity) is nonzero for Re s > 0, so the completed L-function vanishes at s; the functional equation (Mathlib's completedLFunction_one_sub, applied to χ⁻¹, which is primitive since its conductor is that of χ) gives L(χ⁻¹, 1 − s) = 0. If Re s > 1/2 the half-plane statement rules out L(χ, s) = 0 directly; if Re s < 1/2 then Re(1 − s) > 1/2 and it rules out L(χ⁻¹, 1 − s) = 0. So Re s = 1/2. This is the reflection step the blueprint describes.

readings.summary: Read Claim.strip and Claim.prim_zero. prim_zero: for 0 < Re s < 1, a zero of L(χ, s) is a zero of L(χ*, s), with χ* the primitive character inducing χ, because L(χ) = L(χ*) · ∏_{p | N} (1 − χ*(p) p^(−s)) and each Euler factor is nonzero when Re s > 0. Claim.strip then applies the primitive case. claimAll packages HalfPlane, Strip and Zeta together. Matches the blueprint proof.

readings.summary: Traced LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re := allChi := UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter, which is everyCharacter_of_row applied to the proved term galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter. So the half-plane theorem is closed: no hypothesis is left open at the top level. The blueprint's summary of how it is proved (Galois representations, then a Tate–Shafarevich bound, then theta lifts and families, then Landau's theorem) is the route the statements below take; this reading checked only the top of the chain.

readings.summary: Traced Main.riemannHypothesis := rhOfAll := Formalism.VW.rh_of_every allChi. rh_of_every takes χ = 1 mod 1 to get ζ(s) ≠ 0 for Re s > 1/2, then rh_of_right, a Mathlib-only file, reflects. Suppose ζ(s) = 0 with s not a trivial zero and s ≠ 1. If Re s > 1/2 that contradicts the half-plane statement. If Re s < 1/2, Mathlib's riemannZeta_one_sub (at 1 − s) writes ζ(s) as 2(2π)^(−(1−s)) Γ(1−s) cos(π(1−s)/2) ζ(1−s); the proof checks each factor before ζ(1−s) is nonzero (the cosine vanishes only at the trivial zeros, and s = 0 is excluded by ζ(0) = −1/2), so ζ(1−s) = 0 with Re(1−s) > 1/2, again a contradiction. Hence Re s = 1/2. Matches the blueprint proof step for step.

readings.summary: Read UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive. From zero-freeness for primitive characters it gets it for all, using Mathlib's LFunction_changeLevel: L(χ, s) = L(χ*, s) · ∏_{p | N} (1 − χ*(p) p^(−s)), and |χ*(p) p^(−s)| < 1 when Re s > 0, so no Euler factor vanishes. The Lean needs this only for Re s > 1/2. Matches the blueprint, which states it as a published (classical) fact.

readings.summary: Read UpperTheory.Lit.every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching. It takes seven hypotheses: UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses, ThetaLocalInputs, ThetaIntegralsAgree, LocalMatching, CovolumeBoundOfX, RecTExists and VWin. The blueprint statement names only the Tate–Shafarevich bound (and the Galois representations through its proof). The first two are built from published results (published_results_eigen and published_results_first), and the blueprint's house rule is to leave those out of statements. That is fine. But ThetaIntegralsAgree, LocalMatching and CovolumeBoundOfX are results of this proof (chapters on theta lifts and heights), and a reader of the statement alone would not know the theorem depends on them. Not a mismatch in mathematics; a gap in the account. Suggest the statement or its proof name these three inputs with links. I did not trace where each is proved.

readings.summary: Read UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v_win and every_character_of_green_v_win. Hypotheses: GLq.Green, VWin, and a nonempty HypsAlt (the family hypotheses, i.e. def-family-data). Conclusion: ZeroFreeAll, then EveryCharacter. readings.summary: Read VWin, VWinAt, VVle, WinPair, PageN and IsChiField. The conditions match: q ≡ 3 mod 8, d ≡ 7 mod 16, q | d + 1, every odd p ≤ Y^(ε/5) divides d + 1, ε < 1/52, Y between X^(1/J) and X^(1/2), x between Y and Y², t = ⌊x^401⌋, and the bound √(exp(x^ε)) = e^(x^ε/2). Where the blueprint writes ≍, the Lean is explicit: log q in (Y^(ε/5)/2, Y^(ε/5)] and log d in (Y^(ε/5) log²Y / 2, Y^(ε/5) log²Y]. The Lean also asks for the bound for every choice of exponent e with 2^e in [x^(2+8ε), 2x^(2+8ε)], every algebraic closure and every choice of local data, and sums Tate–Shafarevich lengths over 1 ≤ e < t. These are precise forms of the blueprint's statement, not changes to it.

readings.summary: Read IsRecT, LawsT and TypeLaw. LawsT's fields match the blueprint's bullets: dim; one (characters go through the local Artin map); langlands (segments); cusp (cuspidal to irreducible); nu (twists by |det|^s); twist, central, dual, inj and depth for good representations; and type (the tame parameter of a depth-zero cuspidal inflated from a Green character, with N = 0). Two small differences: (1) LawsT also has absCentral, for every representation, saying the absolute value of the determinant matches the central character; the blueprint lists central characters only for good ones. (2) The Lean's local fields are completions of number fields at finite places, so p-adic fields only, while the blueprint says any non-archimedean local field. Neither changes how it is used.

readings.summary: The remark says the blueprint authors have not checked that each use of the Galois representations needs only the weak compatibility. Reading LawsT confirms that the system is weak: only characters and twists of depth-zero cuspidals over Q_g (and representations built from them) are 'good', and other cuspidals get any irreducible parameter of the right dimension. One point worth stating: the formal proof cannot use more than this, because the Lean kernel accepted every step with IsRecT as defined. So the open check is about the blueprint's prose proofs, not the formal one: does any prose proof quietly use full local–global compatibility? That still needs a reader going through each use. Logged as a concern so it stays visible.

readings.summary: Read Row0b up to its conclusion: for a CM field E, a prime l, ι : Q̄_l ≅ C and a ≥ 1, every regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_a with a polarizing Hecke character χ of the maximal real subfield gets r : G_E → GL_a(Q̄_l), a weight and Hodge–Tate multisets satisfying PropsB. That shape matches the blueprint. I stopped at PropsB, which carries the Hodge–Tate, l ∤ w and l | w conditions the blueprint lists; I have not read it, so I can't say the three bullets match. The next reader should start at PropsB in WeightsConjBis.lean and compare it with Row0's Props (WeightsConjAlt.lean) to see what 'weakened' means exactly.
